stories.headline: Swedish voters leave election in tight deadlock between political blocs
stories.body:
Swedish voters cast ballots in a closely fought election that could bring the far-right into government.

Sweden is a Nordic nation. The country has a population of 10.6 million people.

Public broadcaster SVT said the two main political blocs were separated by only 20,000 votes. This gap was recorded with 50% of the votes counted.

Projected results from Sweden's election authority gave Magdalena Andersson's left-wing bloc a one-seat majority. Her Social Democrat-led group led over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's coalition.

At 9:45pm local time, SVT projected the opposition bloc leading by 175 seats to 174 seats.

Christian Democrats leader Ebba Busch said the election result may remain uncertain until Wednesday. Swedish Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard also said results might not be clear until Wednesday. She explained that election officials are waiting for overseas votes to arrive.

Under Prime Minister Kristersson, Sweden made several major policy changes. Sweden abolished permanent residency for refugees. The government also tightened welfare rules. In addition, authorities increased expulsions.

Kristersson promised cabinet jobs to the hard-right Sweden Democrats if he remains in office. The Sweden Democrats were founded by Nazi sympathisers in the 1980s.

Partial election results suggest the Sweden Democrats lost support for the first time since 2010. The party first entered parliament in 2010. Party leader Jimmie Åkesson acknowledged his party lost percentage points compared to 2022. He said the party likely lost its status as Sweden's second-largest party. While voting in the suburb of Rinkeby, Åkesson remarked that it "doesn't look like Sweden".

Andersson questioned voters about the future of the nation. She asked if Sweden should have a government entirely dominated by the Sweden Democrats. She said such a outcome has never happened in Sweden before. She asked if voters wanted a government led by her instead. She said her government would steer Sweden in a new spirit of co-operation.

Projected vote shares showed the Social Democrats leading with 27.6%. The Moderates followed with 20.0%. The Sweden Democrats received 17.5%. The Left Party won 8.2%. The Centre Party reached 7.1%. The Christian Democrats achieved 6.3%. The Green Party received 6.2%. The Liberals got 5.5%.

Liberal Party leader Simona Mohamsson called her party's election results a historic comeback.

Sweden is a Nordic nation with a population of 10.6 million people.

Projected results from Sweden's election authority gave Magdalena Andersson's Social Democrat-led left-wing bloc a one-seat majority over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's coalition.
SVT's projection at 9:45pm local time showed the opposition bloc leading the government parties by 175 seats to 174 seats.
Christian Democrats leader Ebba Busch stated that the election result may remain uncertain until Wednesday.
Swedish Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard stated that election results might not be clear until Wednesday when overseas votes arrive.
Under Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, Sweden abolished permanent residency for refugees, tightened welfare rules, and increased expulsions.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson promised cabinet jobs to the hard-right Sweden Democrats if he remains in office.
The Sweden Democrats were founded by Nazi sympathisers in the 1980s.
Partial election results suggest the Sweden Democrats lost support for the first time since entering parliament in 2010.
Sweden Democrats leader Jimmie Åkesson acknowledged his party lost percentage points compared to 2022 and likely lost its status as Sweden's second-largest party.
While voting in Rinkeby, Sweden Democrats leader Jimmie Åkesson remarked that the suburb "doesn't look like Sweden".

Magdalena Andersson asked after voting: "Should we have a government entirely dominated by the Sweden Democrats, something that has never happened in Sweden before? Or should we have a government led by me, which will steer Sweden in a new spirit of co-operation?"

Projected vote shares showed Social Democrats at 27.6%, Moderates at 20.0%, Sweden Democrats at 17.5%, Left Party at 8.2%, Centre Party at 7.1%, Christian Democrats at 6.3%, Green Party at 6.2%, and Liberals at 5.5%.
Liberal Party leader Simona Mohamsson called her party's election results "a historic comeback".

stories.headline: Six dead and over 100 missing after ferry capsizes in Indonesia's Java Sea
stories.body:
Rescue teams searched for over 100 missing people after a ferry capsized in Indonesia's Java Sea.

The passenger ferry Virgo Transport 8 carried 213 passengers and 30 crew members. France 24 reported that the ferry carried 243 people between Java and Borneo. Six people died and 107 were rescued. But France 24 reported at least one person died. At least 130 people were reported missing after contact was lost during bad weather. France 24 reported more than 100 people remained missing.

The vessel departed Surabaya at 10:33 on Saturday. It was scheduled to reach Banjarmasin at 14:00 on Sunday. The Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office received a report two hours after losing contact at about 2am Sunday.

Indonesian Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said helicopter surveillance confirmed the ferry capsized but had not sunk by 3pm. Search and rescue chief I Putu Sudayana said rescue ships fought waves up to 2.5 metres high.

The 119-metre ferry was built in Japan in 1987. It was operated by PT Virgo Karya Shipping. The ship was carrying 89 vehicles.

Government data shows 111 ship accidents were recorded in Indonesia between 2020 and 2026. Four days earlier, a ferry fire in the Philippines killed at least 76 people.

The Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office received a report two hours after contact was lost with the Virgo Transport 8 at about 2am Sunday.

A passenger ferry fire in the Philippines four days prior killed at least 76 people with 10 others missing.

stories.headline: Russian drone strikes Ukrainian passenger train near Polish border
stories.body:
Russian forces launched a jet-propelled drone that struck a Ukrainian passenger train running between Kyiv and Warsaw near the Polish border.

The drone hit the locomotive at Yahodyn after an evacuation order was given 15 minutes earlier. The strike occurred two kilometres from the border.

Former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson was at the Yagodyn station nearby around the time of the attack. Former CIA Director David Petraeus was also at the station. Railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said a diplomatic train carrying Johnson departed early due to timetable changes. Former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt said passengers on his train prepared for evacuation before arriving safely in Poland.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the strike was terror knocking at the doors of the EU and Nato. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that he expects Russia to escalate the war. Russia's Defence Ministry said strikes targeted railway infrastructure transporting European military cargo.

Overnight Russian attacks using over 450 drones and missiles killed at least six people across Ukraine. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 405 drones and four missiles.

Former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson and former CIA Director David Petraeus were at the Yagodyn border station nearby around the time of the attack.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha characterized the strike near the Polish border as "Putin's terror 'knocking' directly on the doors of the EU and Nato".
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned following an emergency meeting that he expects Russia to escalate the war in coming weeks.
Russia's Defence Ministry stated its strikes targeted railway infrastructure used to transport European military cargo.
Overnight Russian attacks using over 450 drones and missiles killed at least six people across Ukraine, while Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 405 drones and four missiles.

stories.headline: Oil prices surge following military strikes on Saudi Arabia and Gulf shipping
stories.body:
Houthi militants attacked Saudi oil pipelines and ships in the Gulf, driving up global energy prices.

Brent crude futures rose $3.62 to $108.23 per barrel after the strikes. WTI crude futures rose $3.15 to $103.20 per barrel.

An attack on an Iranian cargo ship off Qeshm Island killed one person and wounded four others. The UKMTO reported a severe fire on a vessel hit by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. About one-fifth of world oil and LNG passed through the strait before war broke out on February 28.

Scheduled negotiations in Oman between Iran and Gulf Arab states were postponed. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi announced on X that the meeting was postponed for consensus. Iranian state media said the postponement was a joint decision requested by regional countries.

Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Saudi Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud in New Delhi. They discussed militant attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline. Iraq said recent attacks on the pipeline were launched from Iraqi territory.

stories.headline: United States defeats France to win 12th Women's Basketball World Cup
stories.body:
The United States basketball team defeated France 97-79 in Berlin to win the Women's Basketball World Cup.

The win gave the US team its 12th World Cup title. France led the US by two points at halftime. France opened a 14-point lead early in the second quarter after a 21-2 run. But the US outscored France 30-12 in the third quarter.

Breanna Stewart scored a game-high 22 points for the US. Jackie Young scored 18 points. Caitlin Clark scored 12 points in the final after scoring one point in the semifinal. For France, Gabby Williams scored 16 points in the first half and four in the second half.

France earned silver in its first World Cup final appearance. The US extended its unbeaten run at the Olympics and World Cups to 20 years. The team secured its fifth consecutive World Cup title. The US has not lost a World Cup match since 2006, extending its streak to 36 wins.

Spain won bronze by defeating Germany 81-58. Point guard Iyana Martin scored 20 points for Spain.

Caitlin Clark scored 12 points for the US in the final after scoring one point in the semifinal.
Gabby Williams scored 16 points in the first half and four points in the second half for France.

stories.headline: World leaders gather in New Delhi for BRICS summit on global reforms and cooperation
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Chinese President Xi Jinping at the BRICS summit in New Delhi.

The two leaders held discussions on the sidelines of the summit on September 12, 2026. Prime Minister Modi spoke to President Xi about their shared border. He said peace in border areas remains an essential basis for bilateral relations. He added that tranquility in those areas is necessary for the continued development of ties.

BRICS member nations signed a major document called the New Delhi Declaration 2026. The declaration called for reforms to the UN Security Council. It also called for greater participation of developing economies in global decision-making.

China and Russia again stated support for two key member nations. They backed the aspirations of Brazil and India to play a greater role in the United Nations. This support includes a larger role on the UN Security Council.

During the final session of the summit, Prime Minister Modi raised warnings about global risks. He warned world leaders against the weaponisation of technology. He also warned against the weaponisation of critical minerals.

India served as the host nation for the summit under four foundational pillars. The four pillars of India's BRICS chairship were resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability.

Prime Minister Modi also held a meeting with Philippines President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on September 13, 2026. The two leaders agreed to expand bilateral cooperation across key sectors. They agreed to work together more closely in defence. They agreed to expand security cooperation. They also agreed to deepen ties in trade and space.

In addition, Prime Minister Modi held bilateral meetings on the margins of the summit with several African and Asian leaders. He met with the leader of South Africa. He spoke with the leader of Kazakhstan. He held discussions with the leader of Uganda. He met with the leader of Nigeria. He also held talks with the leader of Burundi.

stories.headline: Indian crew member missing after oil tanker attack off Oman coast
stories.body:
India condemned an attack on a Panama-flagged oil tanker off the coast of Oman.

The attack targeted the MT El Gaia on September 13, 2026. Thirteen Indian crew members of the ship were rescued. Search and rescue operations continued for one missing Indian seafarer.

During the BRICS summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed a Seafarers' Emergency Support Network. The proposal aims to safeguard mariners working in conflict zones.

Indian seafarers account for over 12% of the global merchant shipping workforce. They comprise nearly 312,000 of the world's 2.57 million seafarers. Ten Indian seafarers are among 16 Indians killed in the West Asia conflict. Another five Indian seafarers have died in strikes on merchant vessels in the Black Sea.

In a separate event, an Iranian cargo vessel was struck near Qeshm Island on September 13, 2026. The strike in the Strait of Hormuz left one person dead and four injured. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said the strait would open if the United States terminates its blockade.

stories.headline: India wins Women's Asia Cup but declines trophy from tournament chief
stories.body:
The Indian women's cricket team defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in Dubai to win the Women's Asia Cup.

The victory on September 13, 2026, marked a record-extending eighth title for the team. Shafali Verma scored 68 runs off 39 balls. Smriti Mandhana scored 59 runs off 39 balls. Together they built a 129-run opening partnership for India. Indian bowler Shree Charani took four wickets for 20 runs. Sri Lanka were bowled out for 111.

The Indian team refused to collect the trophy from Asian Cricket Council President Mohsin Naqvi. Naqvi is also Pakistan's interior minister. Indian head coach Amol Muzumdar said the decision was made by the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

The Indian men's cricket team similarly declined to receive the Asia Cup trophy from Naqvi in September 2025. Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu accepted the runners-up cheque from Naqvi during the presentation ceremony.
